payload.rebuttal: fixed: test_an_append_the_record_refuses_emits_no_event only checked that the one event emitted before the refusal had fact_kind == "finding", which both findings in the call share. A record_findings loop that appends its facts in reversed order still emits exactly one finding-kind event before the refusal lands, so the test passed under that mutant. I added an assertion on the specific content of the fact the record actually took (refuse_finding.taken[-1].payload["claim"] == "claim one"), which names the first finding by its own claim text. Under the reversed-order mutant the taken fact is now the second finding (claim "claim two"), so the assertion fails. Verified by reapplying the exact mutant and confirming the witness fails, then restoring saffron/ledger.py and re-running the full suite green.
